lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: even and odd behavior

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: Classify f(x) = x⁴ − 3x² + 1 as even, odd, or neither, and state the corresponding symmetry.
choices: even; its graph is symmetric about the y-axis
neither even nor odd
even; its graph is symmetric about the origin
odd; its graph is symmetric about the origin

items.prompt: The graph of y = f(x) is transformed to y = f(x) + 4. Describe the transformation.
choices: a horizontal compression by a factor of 4
a horizontal shift right by 4
a vertical stretch by a factor of 4
a vertical shift up by 4

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: For f(x) = 4x + 10 and its inverse f⁻¹, evaluate f⁻¹(f(7)).
Classify f(x) = x⁵ + x³ as even, odd, or neither, and state the corresponding symmetry.
choices: odd; its graph is symmetric about the origin
even; its graph is symmetric about the origin
neither even nor odd
even; its graph is symmetric about the y-axis

items.prompt: The graph of y = f(x) is transformed to y = f(x) + 2. Describe the transformation.
choices: a horizontal shift right by 2
a vertical shift up by 2
a horizontal compression by a factor of 2
a vertical stretch by a factor of 2

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: For f(x) = -2x − 1 and its inverse f⁻¹, evaluate f⁻¹(f(-1)).
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
